answer: Resonance-Weighted Coordination Peaks. Each agent's influence scales with the inverse of its cluster's density on a shared basalt substrate, so identities packed tightly around one ridge produce diminishing marginal voice per key. An attacker must spread registered identities across sparse regions and sustain independent actions to avoid the density penalty, paying real compute and registration costs per identity while gaining ever less sway. The mechanism taxes orchestration itself: mass-produced sybils collapse into a dune of near-zero weight.
